To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TOA plays a critical role in avoidance of a taste when it is paired with either a preferred sucrose or a drug of abuse, but not when it is paired to an aversive agent.
bilateral lesions of the TOA disrupt, but do not eliminate, avoidance of a gustatorily conditioned cue when paired with a preferred sucrose or LiCl solution.

In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain mediates the devaluation of natural rewards that accompanies addiction.
how the brain evaluates and compares natural and drug rewards and the role of the gustatory system in these processes.
the neural substrates of natural and drug reward and the neural basis for the apparent devaluation of natural rewards that occurs during addiction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gustatory thalamic nucleus, the gustatory cortex, and the TOA each make a unique contribution to the avoidance of a taste that predicts a natural or drug reward.
the TOA is critical for the development of conditioned taste avoidance in the presence of a drug reward, but not in the presence of natural rewards.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thalamic orosensory system is critical for natural, but not drug, reward.
the TOA plays a necessary role in the development of avoidance of a taste that predicts access to an experimenter-administrered drug of abuse, but not a preferred sucrose.
the TOA is a necessary, but not sufficient, substrate for the development of a taste aversion to a drug of addiction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a bilateral lesion of the TOA disrupts the development of conditioned avoidance of a taste when it predicts access to a drug reward, but not a natural one.
the TOA plays a role in the suppression of natural reward, but not drug reward, in the reward comparison paradigm.
the thalamic gustatory and orosensory nuclei are important for avoidance of a gustory cue that comes to signal access to natural and to drug rewards.
